task.title: Club sign-up form
task.html: Sign up for the programming club
task.description: Bring the form #signup-form to life with jQuery. The practice "server" sendApplication(data, onSuccess) already exists: it takes the data and calls onSuccess after one second. 1) Write showError($field, text): the text goes into the field's error element (its id is in the field's aria-describedby) and the field gets aria-invalid="true"; clearError($field): empty text and no aria-invalid. 2) Write validateForm(): it checks all fields at once and returns true or false. The name after trim() is not empty ("Enter your name") and not shorter than 2 characters ("Name - at least 2 characters"); the email contains @ ("Enter an email with the @ symbol"); the age is a number from 14 to 60 inclusive ("Age - a number from 14 to 60"); a track is selected in #direction ("Choose a track"); the checkbox #agree is checked ("Confirm that you agree to the rules"). For correct fields, the error is cleared. 3) The handler $form.on("submit", ...): cancels the browser's submission, clears #form-message and validates the form. 4) If there are no errors: blocks #submit-btn and writes "Sending..." on it, calls sendApplication($form.serializeArray(), function). In the function: the text "Thank you, Anna! You are signed up for: Web development." in #form-message (the name after trim and the text of the selected track), the form is reset, the button is available again with the text "Sign up". Do not use document.querySelector, innerHTML, .html() or .submit(fn).

hints: The error element of a field: $(`#${$field.attr("aria-describedby")}`) - for #name it is #name-error.
To show all errors at once, do not return after the first one: let isValid = true; ... isValid = false; ... return isValid;
Age: const age = Number($age.val()); it is an error if $age.val() === "", Number.isNaN(age), age < 14 or age > 60.
Checkbox: $agree.prop("checked"). Its .val() is always "on", even when it is not checked.
Text of the selected track: $direction.find("option:checked").text(); jQuery has no .reset() - call $form[0].reset().
Save the name and the track for the message BEFORE calling sendApplication: after reset() the fields are already empty.

questions.question: Why is the handler attached to the form's submit event and not to the button's click?
options: click on a button does not work in jQuery 4
submit fires both on the button and on Enter in a field
submit fires before the page loads
questions.explanation: A form can be submitted with the button or with the Enter key - submit catches both ways.

questions.question: What does $("#agree").val() return for the checkbox <input type="checkbox" id="agree"> without a value attribute if it is NOT checked?
questions.explanation: .val() of a checkbox is its value, not its state. Without a value attribute it is "on". Whether the checkbox is checked - .prop("checked").

questions.question: Which code finds out whether the checkbox #agree is checked right now?
questions.explanation: .prop and :checked read the current state. attr is the original attribute from the HTML, val is the value.

questions.question: Form: name = Anna, age = 20, the agree checkbox is not checked. What does $form.serializeArray() return?
options: [{ name: "name", value: "Anna" }, { name: "age", value: 20 }, { name: "agree", value: false }]
questions.explanation: serializeArray is an array of { name, value } pairs, the values are strings, and an unchecked checkbox is not included.

questions.question: Which jQuery method turns a form into a string like name=%D0%90%D0%BD%D0%BD%D0%B0&age=20? Enter the method name without the dot and brackets.
questions.explanation: .serialize() gives a string to send to the server (lesson 9), .serializeArray() gives an array of objects.

questions.question: What will the code print? const age = $("#age").val(); console.log(typeof age); - the user typed 25 in a type="number" field.
questions.explanation: The value of any field is a string. To compare it, convert it with Number().

questions.question: Match the task with the code.
questions.explanation: jQuery has no .reset() method: you call it on the DOM element of the form.

questions.question: What makes a good error message in a form?
options: It is next to the field and says what to fix
It is linked to the field with aria-describedby
It disappears when the field is fixed
questions.explanation: alert gets in the way and does not show which field is wrong. An error is next to the field, linked to it and disappears after fixing.

questions.question: Why block the submit button while the application is being sent?
options: So that the form is not validated
So that the user does not send the application twice and can see that sending is in progress
questions.explanation: An impatient user clicks the button again - without blocking, two applications are sent.

questions.question: Code: if (name === "") { ... return false; } if (!email.includes("@")) { ... }. The user left both the name and the email empty. How many errors will they see?
questions.explanation: return leaves the function after the first error. To show all errors, collect the result in let isValid = true.

questions.question: Which form attribute turns off the browser's built-in hints so that your code shows the errors? Enter the attribute name.
questions.explanation: <form novalidate> - your script does the checking and writes the error texts, the same in all browsers.

questions.question: Match the field with how to find out what the user chose.
pairs: .val() - the value of the selected option
Text of the selected list item
questions.explanation: For a list, .val() gives the item's value, and the visible label is the .text() of the selected option.
